the PSCLC with negative dielectric is a very promising candidate for a new type of tunable optical device.
the effect of the thickness of the PSCLC cell is to increase the DC field strength required to induce the reflection notch to shift from its original wavelength position to longer wavelengths.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PSCLC devices with negative dielectric liquid crystal material and thin cell thickness can be tuned to a wide range of reflection wavelength by applying a low DC field, and the tuning range and the response time can be adjusted by the cell thickness.
we are able to control the position and bandwidth (or the color and the brightness) of the selective reflection of the polymer stabilized cholesteric LC by applying a direct-current (dc) voltage.

The main takeaway from our work is that

by using a thin PSCLC cell with negative dielectric liquid crystals, a unique and reversible electrically tunable notch filter with high reflectance (≥80% at 0 V) and a wide bandwidth can be achieved.
the DC field strength required to achieve a desired reflection wavelength is a function of the cell thickness, with the thinner cells being easier to tune.
the thickness of a PSCLC cell can be optimized to provide the best performance for a given application.
